newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky nears first execution in 35 years.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky nears first execution in 35 years.

text.p: A 44-year-old convicted killer was to die in Kentucky's electric chair just after midnight on Monday night in what would be the state's first execution in 35 years.
Lawyers for Harold McQueen were working on two last-minute appeals, including one to the U.S. Supreme Court; but prison officials said McQueen was resigned and ready to die if the appeals failed.
He was convicted of killing Rebecca O'Hearn, a store clerk, in 1980 during a robbery while he said he was high on drugs.

His execution at the stone, fortress-like Kentucky State Penitentiary would be the first in the state since 1962 -- 10 years before the U.S. Supreme Court outlawed capital punishment in 1972, a ban it reversed four years later.
More than 160 other men were executed at the prison in earlier years.
A number of prayer vigils were planned by capital punishment opponents in Eddyville and elsewhere.
